title: A Large Language Model Guided Topic Refinement Mechanism for Short Text Modeling
task: Improving topics from any base model on short texts
problem: Short texts give sparse co-occurrence, so mined topics contain semantically intruding words; LLM topic generators need whole documents and do not output bag-of-words topics.
architecture: Model-agnostic post-processing: for each topic, each word is in turn treated as a possible intruder; GPT-3.5-turbo is asked whether it fits the topic of the other words and, if not, proposes 10 alternatives; replacements are chosen iteratively (prompt construction, LLM request/response, iterative refinement).
key_results: Coherence rises for almost all base models and datasets (e.g. Tweet LDA: CP +0.223, UCI +1.452, NPMI +0.086).
Text-classification accuracy improves for every base model (e.g. Tweet accuracy growth 9.70% to 23.19%).
1591.01 input and 274.90 output tokens per topic on Tweet vs 4958.73 and 1214.07 for LLM-TM; on TagMyNews LLM-TM needs 61872.93 input tokens.
strengths: Works with any base model and keeps the bag-of-words topic format, so standard metrics still apply.
Token cost is independent of corpus size because only topic words are sent.

limitations.text: Final quality depends on the initial base topics.
CV slightly decreases for some models (e.g. Tweet: G-BAT -0.012, LLM-TM -0.005); replacement words come from the LLM and may not occur in the corpus vocabulary.

notes: Tested on eight base models plus LLM-TM; K = 20 and 50.
